ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, the pentagon's outer boundary is in order A-B-C-D-E. The right-side triangle ABC is formed by AB, BC and the vertical side AC, and point F is on AC. The left side is composed of triangles AEF, DFE, CDF; line segments EF and DF connect from the left-side points E and D to point F on AC, and DE is part of the left vertical side. According to the figure and the problem statement, ABC is an equilateral triangle, and AEF, DFE, CDF are congruent isosceles triangles. Reasoning: According to the correspondence of the three congruent isosceles triangles in the figure, take AF, DE, CF as corresponding bases, and let AF=DE=CF=b; take AE, EF, DF, CD as corresponding legs, and let AE=EF=DF=CD=a. Because F is on AC, AC=AF+FC=2b. Triangle ABC is an equilateral triangle, so AB=BC=AC=2b, hence its perimeter is 3·2b=6b. The problem says the four triangles all have the same perimeter, so the perimeter 2a+b of each left-side isosceles triangle equals 6b, that is, 2a+b=6b, therefore 2a=5b. The perimeter of pentagon ABCDE is AB+BC+CD+DE+EA=2b+2b+a+b+a=5b+2a=5b+5b=10b. Therefore the ratio of the perimeter of pentagon ABCDE to the perimeter of triangle ABC is 10b/6b=5/3.

raw_record.question_text: The pentagon $ABCDE$ is split into four triangles that all have the same perimeter (see diagram). Triangle $ABC$ is equilateral, and the triangles $AEF$, $DFE$, and $CDF$ are congruent isosceles triangles. How big is the ratio of the perimeter of the pentagon $ABCDE$ to the perimeter of the triangle $ABC$?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the outer pentagon is ordered A-B-C-D-E, with AC drawn vertically inside and point F on AC. The four triangular regions are ABC on the right, and AEF, DFE, CDF on the left. From the visual shape of the three congruent isosceles triangles, take AF, DE, and CF as the corresponding bases, and AE, EF, DF, CD as corresponding equal legs, so let AF=DE=CF=b and AE=EF=DF=CD=a. From the text, ABC is equilateral and all four triangles have the same perimeter. Since AC=AF+FC=2b, the side length of equilateral triangle ABC is 2b, so its perimeter is 6b. The perimeter of any left isosceles triangle is 2a+b, and it equals 6b, giving 2a=5b. The pentagon perimeter is AB+BC+CD+DE+EA=2(2b)+a+b+a=5b+2a=10b. Therefore the desired ratio is 10b/6b=5/3.
